name: Low A tap / strike
notes: Uncommon. Patrick McLaurin describes closing the Low-A finger briefly to sound Low G, but notes that a birl is generally used instead. Prior and target are both Low A. Nether Lorn/Campbell: no standardized standalone tap/strike vocable was found in the consulted scale and movement tables; leave blank pending contextual encoding review.

name: B tap / strike
notes: Close the topmost open lower-hand hole briefly, sounding Low G while B remains the melody note. Prior and target are both B. Nether Lorn/Campbell: no standardized standalone tap/strike vocable was found in the consulted scale and movement tables; leave blank pending contextual encoding review.

name: F tap / strike

name: High A tap / strike

name: Heavy throw on D (literal)

name: Heavy throw on D (abbreviated notation)

name: Light throw on D
notes: Literal light execution of the same Gdc written form: Low G, D gracenote to C, then D. Excludes prior Low G for now. Beat/anchor is the C component.

name: Modern taorluath to Low G — pipe-band anchor

name: High G doubling
notes: Special High-G doubling: High-G gracenote to F, then resolve to High G. Prior note must be F or below. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1; RNZ/solo practice may instead anchor F. Prior-specific piobaireachd bari/dari forms have different patterns and are not conflated here.

name: High A doubling
notes: Special High-A doubling: High-A/thumb gracenote to High G, then resolve to High A. Prior note is below High A. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1. Nether Lorn/Campbell identifies this movement as dili.

name: B slur
notes: Patrick: High-G gracenote to B followed by a Low-G tap/strike. BWW classifies this as a G-gracenote strike. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1.

name: C slur
notes: Patrick: High-G gracenote to C followed by a Low-G tap/strike. BWW classifies this as a G-gracenote strike. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1.

name: D slur — light
notes: Patrick’s light D slur: High-G gracenote to D followed by a C tap/strike. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1.

name: D slur — heavy
notes: Patrick’s heavy D slur: High-G gracenote to D followed by a Low-G tap/strike. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1.

name: E slur
notes: Patrick: High-G gracenote to E followed by a Low-A tap/strike. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1.

name: F slur
notes: Patrick: High-G gracenote to F followed by an E tap/strike. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1.

name: High G slur
notes: Patrick: High-A/thumb gracenote to High G followed by an F tap/strike. BWW places this in the thumb-strike family. Pipe-band timing anchors component 1.

name: B hornpipe shake
notes: Patrick: regular B doubling followed by the B tapping gracenote (Low G). The D-intermediate form is the standard/default variant.

name: B hornpipe shake — E intermediate
notes: Patrick: common alternative B hornpipe shake using E, rather than D, as the intermediate gracenote in the doubling; followed by the B tapping gracenote (Low G).

name: C hornpipe shake
notes: Patrick: regular C doubling followed by the C tapping gracenote (Low G). The D-intermediate form is the standard/default variant.

name: C hornpipe shake — E intermediate

name: D hornpipe shake — light

name: D hornpipe shake — heavy
notes: Patrick: regular D doubling followed by the heavy D tapping gracenote (Low G).

name: E hornpipe shake
notes: Patrick: regular E doubling followed by the E tapping gracenote (Low A).

name: F hornpipe shake
notes: Patrick: regular F doubling followed by the F tapping gracenote (E).

name: Birl
notes: Patrick’s basic birl: two rapid Low-G interruptions resolving to Low A. Physical methods (seven, double tap, tap-drag, swipe) are execution choices, not separate sounding variants.

name: Birl from Low A
notes: Context-explicit form when the preceding melody note is Low A; preserves the initial Low A before the two Low-G interruptions.

name: G-gracenote birl
notes: G-gracenote birl used from notes where a High-G gracenote is available; resolves to Low A. Prior High G instead uses the thumb-gracenote form, and prior High A omits the unavailable opening gracenote.

name: High-A-gracenote birl
notes: Thumb/High-A-gracenote birl used from preceding High G; resolves to Low A.

name: Pele on Low A
notes: Full Low-A pele with High-G opening. Regular form applies from notes where the opening High-G gracenote is available.

name: Thumb pele on Low A
notes: Thumb form used from preceding High G.

name: Half pele on Low A
notes: Half form used from preceding High A; opening gracenote is omitted.

name: Half pele on C

name: Pele on D — open

notes: Half closed form from preceding High A; final tap is Low G.

name: Half pele on D — open

name: Half pele on High G

name: Bubbly note / darodo
notes: Standard light-music darodo: three Low Gs separated by D and C gracenotes.

name: Darodo — piobaireachd
notes: Same movement with even piobaireachd source timing.

name: Darodo — 16th-note style
notes: Darodo timing variant with longer outer Low-G components.

name: Darodo from Low G
notes: Contextual half form when the preceding melody note is already Low G; the initial Low G is not repeated.

name: B-opening bubbly note
notes: Distinct light-music bubbly-note form opening with a High-G gracenote to B, then Low G–C–Low G. It is not conflated with the traditional darodo name.

name: Half D throw
notes: Half/light D throw from preceding Low G. The initial Low G of the full light throw is supplied by the preceding melody note, leaving D gracenote to C before resolving to D.

name: D-to-C tachum
notes: Jim McGillivray model: a short D introduced by a High-G gracenote, followed by the longer lower C introduced by a D gracenote. This is a two-note Scotch-snap figure; the destination note is stored separately as target_note. Canntaireachd left blank: no attested traditional tachum form has yet been established; do not construct one merely by concatenating scale vocables.

name: Rodin
notes: Piobaireachd rodin: two Low Gs separated by a B gracenote, resolving to Low A. Use the prior-specific harodin or horodin row when the preceding note is D or C.

name: Harodin
notes: Traditional D-to-Low-A rodin context. The movement is two Low Gs separated by B, then resolves to Low A.

name: Horodin
notes: Traditional C-to-Low-A rodin context. The movement is two Low Gs separated by B, then resolves to Low A.

name: Otro — B-to-B

The final B is stored separately as target_note, so pattern gBGdG plus target B represents the complete B-to-B movement. Traditional naming correction in the video description confirms B-to-B is otro. prior_note=* excludes High G and High A, which use the contextual rows below. Timing values remain nominal.

name: Thumb otro — B-to-B

name: Hiharin
notes: Hiharin: passing D gracenote on Low A followed by a birl; resolves to Low A. Target corrected from Low G to Low A.

name: Dre
notes: Jim McGillivray reference: dre is the lower-note approach to the E–Low A–F–Low A–E movement. Pattern eAf plus target E is the correct stored expansion. The opening E carries the beat and is slightly broader than the following internal notes, reflected by nominal ratio 2,1,1 and anchor 1. prior_note=* is constrained to Low G, Low A, B, C, or D; a future parser should encode that range explicitly rather than rely only on this note. Cross-reference: McGillivray 2026 Piobaireachd Practice Pack.

name: Edre
notes: Jim McGillivray reference: edre is the upper-note approach to the same E–Low A–F–Low A–E movement. Pattern eAf plus target E is the correct stored expansion. The opening E carries the beat and is naturally more exposed from the upper hand, reflected by nominal ratio 2,1,1 and anchor 1. prior_note=* is constrained to F, High G, or High A; a future parser should encode that range explicitly rather than rely only on this note. Cross-reference: McGillivray 2026 Piobaireachd Practice Pack.

name: Dare

name: Vedare
notes: Vedare from a higher note: brief F followed by the F-to-E / High-G-grace figure, resolving to F. Prior wildcard is constrained in practice to notes above F. Cross-reference: McGillivray 2026 Piobaireachd Practice Pack.

name: Standard crunluath
notes: The theme note is the prior note and carries the beat; the entire crunluath, including its final short E, is part of that prior note. Applies to all theme notes except D and Low G, which use specific rows. Cross-reference: McGillivray 2026 Piobaireachd Practice Pack.

name: Standard crunluath from D
notes: The D theme note is the prior note and carries the beat. B replaces the unavailable internal D gracenote; the final short E remains part of the embellishment. Cross-reference: McGillivray 2026 Piobaireachd Practice Pack.

name: Standard crunluath from Low G
notes: The Low-G theme note is the prior note and carries the beat. Its first Low G is absorbed; the remaining movement has three Low As and includes the final short E. Cross-reference: McGillivray 2026 Piobaireachd Practice Pack.

name: Crunluath Fosgailte
notes: The Low-A theme note is the prior note and carries the beat. The complete fosgailte movement is treated as part of that prior note; target_note and anchor are intentionally blank. Other theme-note forms require separate rows. Cross-reference: McGillivray 2026 Piobaireachd Practice Pack.

name: Crunluath A Mach
